I am an economist-statistician and PhD candidate in Economics at ENSEA. I work
at the intersection of official statistics, public policy, and data science.
Since 2021, I have worked at Côte d’Ivoire’s National Agency of Statistics
(ANSTAT), where I serve as Deputy Director for Innovation, Data, Research and
Methodology and Head of DataLaB, ANSTAT’s data innovation lab. See my
[innovation work](innovation/index.qmd).

My work explores how artificial intelligence, big data, and modern survey
methods can improve economic measurement and public decision-making. I am
particularly interested in labor markets, poverty, and economic development in
Côte d’Ivoire and West Africa.

## Current focus

- **Economic measurement:** labor markets, poverty, education, and household welfare.
- **Doctoral research:** labor-market frictions in Côte d’Ivoire.
- **Statistical innovation:** AI, satellite imagery, big data, and survey methods.
- **Knowledge sharing:** teaching econometrics and sampling, and writing about economics and data.
